Monopoly: Marginal Revenue and Deadweight Loss

The monopolist sets price by sliding down the demand curve — which is why marginal revenue MRMRMR falls twice as fast as demand. Profit peaks where MR=MCMR = MCMR=MC, but the red triangle of welfare on the unproduced output evaporates.

MR(Q)=A−2BQ,Qm=A−c2BMR(Q) = A - 2BQ, \qquad Q_m = \frac{A-c}{2B}MR(Q)=A−2BQ,Qm​=2BA−c​
Pm−cPm=1∣ε∣\frac{P_m - c}{P_m} = \frac{1}{|\varepsilon|}Pm​Pm​−c​=∣ε∣1​

Examples & Exercises

With demand P=10−QP = 10 - QP=10−Q and marginal cost c=2c = 2c=2, compute by hand the monopolist's profit-maximizing quantity, price, profit, and deadweight loss.

MR(Q)=10−2Q,MR=MCMR(Q) = 10 - 2Q, \qquad MR = MCMR(Q)=10−2Q,MR=MC
Qm=A−c2B,Pm=A+c2Q_m = \frac{A-c}{2B}, \quad P_m = \frac{A+c}{2}Qm​=2BA−c​,Pm​=2A+c​
Show proof
  1. Marginal revenue is MR=10−2QMR = 10 - 2QMR=10−2Q. From MR=MCMR = MCMR=MC, 10−2Q=210 - 2Q = 210−2Q=2, so Qm=4Q_m = 4Qm​=4, and on the demand curve Pm=10−4=6P_m = 10 - 4 = 6Pm​=10−4=6.
  2. Profit is (6−2)⋅4=16(6-2) \cdot 4 = 16(6−2)⋅4=16. The competitive quantity is Qc=8Q_c = 8Qc​=8, so deadweight loss is (6−2)(8−4)/2=8(6-2)(8-4)/2 = 8(6−2)(8−4)/2=8 — welfare the monopoly destroys without capturing.
    πm=16,DWL=8=(Pm−c)(Qc−Qm)2\pi_m = 16, \qquad DWL = 8 = \frac{(P_m - c)(Q_c - Q_m)}{2}πm​=16,DWL=8=2(Pm​−c)(Qc​−Qm​)​
